summary: Security review of Task 11 (Playwright E2E i18n spec + Nuxt DevTools disable + bundle.optimizeTranslationDirective=false). Scope: frontend/e2e/i18n.spec.ts (NEW, 21 LOC) and frontend/nuxt.config.ts (additive config changes). No backend code, no auth logic, no user-input handlers, no dependency upgrades. The test exercises client-side validation only — Zod schema blocks the submit on the invalid-email fixture, so POST /api/auth/login never fires and no credentials are transmitted. The fixture value `not-an-email` is a deliberately invalid string and not a real credential. No hardcoded secrets, tokens, or real email addresses anywhere in the spec. `devtools: { enabled: false }` is a dev-only Nuxt setting; @nuxt/devtools is stripped from production builds by Nuxt's build pipeline regardless of this flag, and explicitly disabling it slightly reduces local-dev attack surface (no devtools server/inspector page exposed). `bundle.optimizeTranslationDirective: false` is a build-time perf toggle for the `v-t` directive compile step — it does not change Vue's text-interpolation escaping or any security-relevant code path; v-t and $t both produce escaped text content in Vue. The pre-existing AUTH_HEADERS routeRules (X-Robots-Tag noindex/nofollow + Referrer-Policy no-referrer for /auth/** and /{locale}/auth/**) are preserved and unaffected. No OWASP Top 10 (2021) categories triggered.

non_blocking_findings.title: E2E spec relies on real backend availability via webServer auto-spawn
non_blocking_findings.description: The test assumes the dev server (`pnpm dev`) is auto-spawned by playwright.config.ts and that the backend at NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE (default http://localhost:8080) is either reachable or irrelevant. Since the form blocks at Zod validation, no real backend call is made for THIS spec — confirmed safe. However, future E2E specs added to the same file/suite that DO submit valid emails could leak real credentials to a live backend if a developer accidentally points NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE at staging/prod. Not a defect in this commit; flag for future awareness only.
non_blocking_findings.impact: None for this commit. Forward-looking risk: a future contributor adding a 'happy-path login' spec without route mocking could POST credentials to a non-local backend if env is misconfigured.
non_blocking_findings.recommendation: Consider adding `await page.route('**/api/auth/login', (r) => r.abort())` as a defense-in-depth guard, or document in playwright.config.ts that NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE must be local for E2E. Optional — current spec is safe as-is.

checks_performed.hardcoded_secrets: PASS — fixture `not-an-email` is intentionally invalid; no API keys, tokens, passwords, real emails, or connection strings.
checks_performed.credentials_transmitted: PASS — Zod validation fails on `not-an-email` before form.submit() handler dispatches POST /api/auth/login. Verified by reading task spec (AC: 'Тест не залежить від реального backend — логін НЕ виконується') and the test flow (fill invalid → submit click → assert validation message, no network assertion or response wait).
checks_performed.devtools_production_impact: PASS — devtools is a dev-only Nuxt module; production builds (`nuxt build`) strip it via Nuxt's build pipeline regardless of this flag. Explicitly disabling reduces local dev-server attack surface (no /__nuxt_devtools__ inspector route exposed).
checks_performed.bundle_optimizeTranslationDirective: PASS — build-time perf toggle for v-t directive compilation only. No effect on Vue's HTML-escaping of interpolated text; v-t and $t both render escaped text content. Setting it to false reverts to runtime translation lookup for v-t (which is unused in this codebase per the comment), so XSS posture is unchanged.
checks_performed.owasp_a01_access_control: N/A — no auth/route-rule changes; existing AUTH_HEADERS routeRules preserved.
